summary: Paul Groner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD from Yale University and studied at the University of Tokyo in 1973. His career includes long-term professorial appointments in Religious Studies at the University of Virginia.

Paul Hacker (1913–1979) was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. Educated at Bonn, Heidelberg, Frankfurt, and Berlin, he held the chair for Indology at the University of Bonn (1955–1963) and at the University of Münster (1963–1978).

Paul Harrison (born 1950) works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Auckland and ANU under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana. He taught at Auckland, Canterbury, and later joined the Stanford University faculty.

Paul J. Griffiths (born 1955) specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Oxford and Wisconsin under Minoru Kiyota, he held professorships at the University of Chicago, Notre Dame, the University of Illinois Chicago, and Duke University.
Paul K. Nietupski works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from Columbia University and held a post at John Carroll University (attested 2008).
Paul Kingsbury is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under the supervision of George Cardona (attested 2002).

Paul Kiparsky (born 1941) specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology under Morris Halle from circa 1962 to 1965 and joined the faculty at Stanford University around 1984.

Paul L. Swanson (born 1951) works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He served as a professor at Nanzan University and directed the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture.

Paul Mendes-Flohr (1941–2024) was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and history. After earning his doctorate at Brandeis University, he served as a director at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and as a professor at the University of Chicago.

Paul Mus (1902–1969) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology educated at Paris and EPHE under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at the EFEO, Collège de France (1946–1969), and Yale University.
Paul Passy (1859–1940) was a linguist who studied under Ferdinand de Saussure. He held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1894 to 1913.

Paul Pelliot (1878–1945) specialized in Sinology, Central Asian studies, and Tibetology, studying under Émile Senart, Sylvain Lévi, and Édouard Chavannes. He served as a professor at the EFEO and held the Central Asian chair at the Collège de France (1911–1945).

Paul R. Brass (1936–2022) was an Indology scholar who studied at Harvard College, the University of Chicago, and Harvard University. He was a professor at the University of Washington from circa 1967 to 2001.
Paul Regnaud (1838–1910) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études around 1869 and held a post at the University of Lyon from circa 1879 to 1908.

Paul Ricœur (1913–2005) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Rennes and Paris. His academic career included professorships at the University of Strasbourg, the Sorbonne, Paris Nanterre, Catholic University of Louvain, and the University of Chicago.
Paul Rouzer is a scholar in the fields of Sinology and Buddhist studies. In 2007, he was attested holding posts at both Harvard University and the University of Minnesota.

Paul Tedesco (1898–1980) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Vienna, held a research post at Princeton, and later became a professor of Sanskrit and linguistics at Yale University.

Paul Thieme (1905–2001) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Göttingen and Berlin. He held professorships at Halle-Wittenberg (1941–1953), Frankfurt (1953), Yale University (1954–1960), and the University of Tübingen (1960–1973).

Paul Tillich (1886–1965) was a philosopher and theologian educated at Berlin, Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, and Breslau. He taught at Dresden, Frankfurt, Union Theological Seminary (1933–1955), Harvard University (1955–1962), and the University of Chicago (1962–1965).

Paul W. Kroll (born 1948) is a Sinologist who studied at the University of Michigan from circa 1971 to 1976. He served as Associate Professor of Chinese and department chairman at the University of Colorado Boulder between 1979 and 1989.
